title: A service crashed or restarted
description: Find when it stopped, what it logged just before, and whether it keeps happening.

steps.title: Fatal events
steps.instruction: Any fatal event is the first suspect. Note the first one.

steps.title: Unhandled exceptions
steps.instruction: Events with an exception at error level or worse.

steps.title: Which sources are affected
steps.instruction: Is it one process or many?

action.ql: level >= error | stats count() as errors by @source | sort errors desc | head 10

steps.title: Check the Problems pane
steps.instruction: Truncated or unreadable files can hide the moment of the crash.

steps.title: Read the last events before the first fatal event
steps.instruction: Open the first fatal event in the Moment view and read what came before it.

title: Errors started after a change
description: Separate new errors from the usual ones.

steps.title: All errors
steps.instruction: How many errors are there in total?

action.ql: level >= error | stats count() as errors

steps.title: Most frequent error messages
steps.instruction: Open the query view and group errors by message with Patterns; compare with the period before the change.

steps.title: Timeouts
steps.instruction: Timeouts after a change usually mean a dependency or a setting moved.

steps.title: Compare before and after
steps.instruction: Use Compare with the change time as the boundary.

title: Requests are slow
description: Find slow operations and what they have in common.

steps.title: Events that mention slowness
steps.instruction: Look for slow, timeout or took.

action.ql: level >= warning | stats count() as n by @source | sort n desc | head 10

steps.title: Confirm nothing is failing outright
steps.instruction: Slowness with fatal events is a different incident.

steps.title: Open the Overview
steps.instruction: Slow outliers and rate changes show up in the health check.

title: Sign-in or access failures
description: Who or what is being refused, and is it new.

steps.title: How many
steps.instruction: A few are normal; thousands in minutes are not.

steps.title: Share carefully
steps.instruction: Export the incident report with redaction on: it contains user names and addresses.
